about: Stellar Ascension's whole design in one file: a standalone two-act game made from Civilization VI and Stellaris. Each section is a table: one row per thing, one column per property. Edit here, then run tools/preflight.py and tools/gen.py. Not-applicable cells hold 0, false, [] or "none" on purpose.

rules.about: Global numbers for both acts. Change here, never in code.

rows.desc: Act 1 calendar starts in 4000 BC.
Civ VI tech cost (from the player's install) is multiplied by this.
Civ VI building, wonder and project cost is multiplied by this.
The Spaceport and the space projects cost this much more on top (they are one city's work, so Civ VI's costs would drag).
Act 1 can't run longer than this; at the limit the civ with the most techs is first to space.
Act 1 also ends when the calendar reaches this year (Act 2 starts in 2200): the civs go to space in order of their science.
A city can't be founded within this many tiles of another city (Civ VI's rule).
Tiles a city can work and own around itself.
Each citizen eats this much food a turn.
Science from each citizen, before buildings.
Gold from each citizen, before buildings.
The city's own tile yields at least this much food.
The city's own tile yields at least this much production.
Science from every city's palace or town hall.
Extra gold from the capital.
Extra science from the capital.
Food to grow from size 1 to 2; Civ VI: 15 + 8(n-1) + (n-1)^1.5.
Extra food per size for the next citizen.
Exponent in the growth formula.
Civ VI's Settler cost, before act1_build_cost_mult.
Each Settler costs this much more than the last.
A city needs this many citizens to train a Settler; training one costs a citizen.
Gold per point of production when buying the current build.
When a rival finishes a wonder first, this share of your progress carries over to your next build.
Rivals stop settling at about this many cities on a small map (scaled by map size).
Act 2 calendar starts in 2200.
Act 2 is turn based: each turn is this many months (ships move, worlds grow and fleets fight month by month within it).
Months for a planet to grow one pop (before modifiers).
Food each pop eats a month.
Jobs per district.
One building slot per this many pops (plus one).
Alloys to build an outpost.
Influence to build an outpost.
Months a construction ship takes to build an outpost.
Months a science ship takes to survey a system.
Months from a colony ship landing until the colony is founded.
Influence per month from the capital.
Naval capacity before modifiers.
Months a fleet must hold an enemy system (with no enemy fleet or starbase left) to take it.
AI empires only declare war on someone their fleet is this much stronger than.
After this many months at war, either side accepts peace.
Combat power of a starbase in an owned system.
Pops on a homeworld at the start of Act 2.
Score per pop.
Score per owned system.
Score per Act 2 technology.
Score per point of fleet power.
Owning this share of all colonized and outposted systems, and at least half of every system in the galaxy, after the first 10 years, wins outright.
Civ VI unit cost (from the install) is multiplied by this and by act1_build_cost_mult, as buildings are.
Gold each unit costs a turn: Civ VI's maintenance times this.
Damage dealt by an even fight (Civ VI: 30 HP), scaled by e^(0.04 x strength difference).
HP a unit heals a turn without moving or fighting, in your own territory (10 more in a city).
HP a unit heals a turn without moving or fighting, outside your territory.
City hit points.
HP a city heals a turn when it was not attacked.
City strength: this plus the best land unit the owner could train (tech only), plus 3 for a capital.
Strength a fortified unit gets when defending.
Defending strength on hills, forest or jungle.
Anti-cavalry units' strength against cavalry.
Ranged (non-siege) units' strength against cities is reduced by this (Civ VI).
Upgrading costs this much gold per point of production between the two units.
Act 1 AIs don't declare war before this turn.
Act 1 AIs only declare war on a neighbour their army is this much stronger than.
An Act 1 war lasts at least this many turns before peace.
Share of tiles with a Civ VI resource (bonus, luxury or strategic).
Improvements a Builder can make before it is used up (Civ VI).
Tribal (barbarian) camps placed per 100 land tiles at the start.
A camp sends out a raider every this many turns (at most two each).
Gold for clearing a tribal camp.
Tribal villages (Civ VI goody huts) per 100 land tiles: entering one gives a reward.
Camps stop sending raiders once the most advanced civ reaches this era (0 = Ancient).
Turns for an Act 1 envoy to reach a civ and open relations.
Gold an Act 1 envoy costs.
Two civs meet when one's units or borders come within this many tiles of the other's.
How long an Act 1 trade deal runs.
An Act 1 melee fight where both survive goes on for up to this many more turns (one round a turn) unless a side withdraws.
A unit that withdraws from a fight takes this share of a normal round's damage.
Envoys every empire has in Act 2 (Stellaris).
Months an Act 2 envoy needs to establish communications with a new empire or species.
How long an Act 2 trade deal runs.
Share of a fleet's power dealt as hull damage each month in an Act 2 battle (so battles run over several turns).
Months a fleet that jumps out with emergency FTL is missing before it reappears at its home system.
Share of its ships (rounded down, at least one if any) a fleet loses in an emergency FTL jump.
Act 1: an exotic site gives its empire-wide bonus once at least this many of its six neighbouring tiles are inside your borders too.
Exotic planets placed in each Act 2 galaxy (a random few from the pool).

space_race.about: How hard losing the race to space hits you. Chosen on the setup screen.

rows.name: Relaxed
rows.desc: If a rival reaches space first, they start Act 2 owning the rare star systems made from this map's natural wonders. Nothing else changes.

rows.name: Standard
rows.desc: Rivals who reach space before you also start Act 2 with +15% alloys and +10 naval capacity. Whoever is first owns the rare star systems.

rows.name: Ruthless
rows.desc: If a rival reaches space first, you lose and there is no Act 2. Only the winner of the space race goes to the stars.

difficulties.about: Civ VI's difficulty levels (Act 1): rivals' yields are multiplied. Act 2 has its own AI difficulty (galaxy_difficulties).

rows.name: Settler
rows.desc: Rivals are slow. Learn the game.

rows.name: Chieftain
rows.desc: Rivals are slower than you.

rows.name: Warlord
rows.desc: Rivals are a little slower than you.

rows.name: Prince
rows.desc: Everyone plays by the same numbers.

rows.name: King
rows.desc: Rivals get +15% yields.

rows.name: Emperor
rows.desc: Rivals get +30% yields.

rows.name: Immortal
rows.desc: Rivals get +50% yields.

rows.name: Deity
rows.desc: Rivals get +75% yields.

map_sizes.about: Act 1 map sizes, with the default number of rivals and of Stellaris alien empires that join in Act 2.

rows.name: Small
rows.desc: A short game: 36 x 22 tiles.

rows.name: Standard
rows.desc: The usual game: 46 x 28 tiles.

rows.name: Large
rows.desc: A long game with many rivals: 58 x 34 tiles.

game_lengths.about: How long Act 2 runs before the highest score wins. Each turn is act2_months_per_turn months.

rows.name: Short
rows.desc: Act 2 ends in 2250 (100 turns).

rows.name: Standard
rows.desc: Act 2 ends in 2275 (150 turns).

rows.name: Long
rows.desc: Act 2 ends in 2300 (200 turns).

yields.about: Act 1 yields. Civ VI's culture and faith are folded in: culture counts as science, faith as gold.

rows.name: Food
rows.desc: Grows cities.

rows.name: Production
rows.desc: Builds Settlers, buildings, wonders and projects.

rows.name: Gold
rows.desc: Buys the current build.

rows.name: Science
rows.desc: Researches technologies.

terrains.about: Act 1 terrain. Yields are Civ VI's (Terrain_YieldChanges); mountains can't be worked or settled. ground/ground_fow: Civ VI terrain textures for seen and fogged land (none on water, which is drawn in its colour); overlay: Civ VI strategic-view sprite drawn on top ({n} picks a variant; none for flat land).

features.about: Act 1 features on land tiles. Yields add to the terrain's (Civ VI's Feature_YieldChanges). sprite/sprite_fow: Civ VI strategic-view picture when seen / in fog.

natural_wonders.about: Natural wonders on the Act 1 map. Their tile yields come from Civ VI (culture as science, faith as gold). In Act 2 each becomes a rare star system: whoever reached space first starts owning it, and whoever holds it gets the modifier. DEFAULT covers natural wonders not listed. sprite: Civ VI strategic-view picture (none: its icon is shown).

Cost here is Civ VI's, before act1_build_cost_mult. district: the Civ VI district it stands in (shown on a tile next to the city; none: the city centre); sprite: its strategic-view picture.

projects.about: Act 1 space projects (Civ VI's), built in a city with a Spaceport. Cost is Civ VI's, before act1_build_cost_mult.

rows.desc: Your first satellite. Needed before the Moon Landing.
Completing this ends Act 1: your civilization reaches space.

units.about: Act 1 land units, stone age to space age. Strength, cost, moves, upkeep, tech, resource and upgrade are read from the player's Civ VI (Units, UnitUpgrades); the numbers here are the base game's, used only if the install lacks a value. 'line' sets the role the AI gives it and what it upgrades along.

improvements.about: Act 1 tile improvements a Builder makes (Civ VI's: name, icon and picture from the install). A tile takes one improvement. terrains/features: where it can go; resources: resources it works (any terrain). A tile with woods, rainforest or marsh only takes improvements that list that feature or work its resource.

civ_traits.about: Each civilization's trait, helping in both acts. Its title in game is the civilization's own Civ VI ability name (from the install); these are the effects. Act 1: % to city yields, unit strength and costs, Builder charges, opinion with other civs. Act 2: modifiers.

rows.name: Scholars
rows.desc: +10% science; in space +10% research.

rows.name: Industrious
rows.desc: +10% production; in space +10% minerals.

rows.name: Warlike
rows.desc: Units +3 strength and 15% cheaper; in space +10% ship damage.

rows.name: Expansionist
rows.desc: Settlers 25% cheaper, +5% food; in space +15% pop growth and +25% survey speed.

rows.name: Mercantile
rows.desc: +20% gold; in space +10% energy and better trade deals.

rows.name: Agrarian
rows.desc: +15% food; in space +15% food.

rows.name: Seafarers
rows.desc: Units embark from the start, +5% gold; in space +15% ship speed and +4 naval capacity.

rows.name: Diplomats
rows.desc: Others like you more (+20 opinion), +5% gold; in space +10% unity and one more envoy.

rows.name: Master Builders
rows.desc: +15% toward wonders, +5% production, Builders get an extra charge; in space +15% build speed.

civ_trait_map.about: Which trait each civilization has (civilizations not listed get one picked from their name).

exotic_sites.about: Out-of-this-world sites (Stellaris's deposits), a few per game. Act 1: on the map like natural wonders; the tile yields these and, held with some neighbouring tiles, gives act1_stat empire-wide; holding it at the handoff lets that empire research unlock_tech. Act 2: a few planets carry one; holding the system gives act2_modifier and lets you research unlock_tech.

rows.name: Living Metal Lake
rows.desc: A lake of liquid metal that heals its own scars. Its people learn from it: in space it opens Regenerative Hull Tissue, and later Living Metal.

rows.name: Exotic Gas Swamp
rows.desc: Bubbling marsh gases with odd chemistry. In space it opens Exotic Gas Refining.

rows.name: Crystalline Caverns
rows.desc: Caves of singing crystal. In space it opens Crystal-Infused Plating.

rows.name: Liquid Dark Matter Pool
rows.desc: A pool that bends light. In space it opens Dark Matter Power, and with Zero Point Power, Dark Matter Deflectors.

rows.name: Nanite Fields
rows.desc: Dust that rebuilds whatever falls into it. In space it opens Nanite Transmutation.

rows.name: Precursor Ruins
rows.desc: The ruins of someone who came before. In space it opens Archaeostudies.

rows.name: Zro Spore Forest
rows.desc: Glowing fungi whose spores bring strange dreams. In space it opens Psionic Theory.

rows.name: Volatile Mote Storm
rows.desc: Unstable particles that burst on contact. Its armies learn to use them (+2 unit strength); in space it opens Mote Stabilization.

rows.name: Electrified Oceans
rows.desc: A sea alive with lightning. In space it opens Field Modulation.

preftl_techs.about: Act 1's pre-FTL research (Stellaris's starting technologies): researched like Civ VI techs once their prerequisites are known. 'core' ones are needed for the Moon Landing; every one you have becomes a known technology in Act 2 (the rest can be researched there).

tech_legacy.about: Civ VI techs that carry a Space Age legacy: each one you research gives its modifier at the start of Act 2. The tech's tooltip names it.

eras.about: Act 1 calendar: the year follows the most advanced civilization's progress through Civ VI's eras, so the space age arrives in the 20th century however fast the game goes. city_sprite: how cities look in that era (Civ VI strategic view; {v} is Visible or Revealed).

resources.about: Act 2 resources (Stellaris's). Research is one pool here.

rows.name: Energy
rows.desc: Upkeep for ships and buildings.

rows.name: Minerals
rows.desc: Builds districts, buildings and ships' hulls.

rows.name: Food
rows.desc: Pops eat it; colony ships carry it.

rows.name: Alloys
rows.desc: Builds warships and outposts.

rows.name: Research
rows.desc: Researches Act 2 technologies.

rows.name: Unity
rows.desc: Adds to your score.

rows.name: Influence
rows.desc: Claims new systems with outposts.

planet_classes.about: Act 2 planet classes (Stellaris's; icon and name from the install). Habitable planets can be colonized; the rest only count for the system.

districts.about: Act 2 planet districts (Stellaris's). Each gives act2_district_jobs jobs; a planet has room for one district per 3 sizes.

rows.desc: Housing and admin: unity, and room for more pops.
Technicians make energy.
Miners dig minerals.
Farmers grow food.
Metallurgists make alloys (each uses 3 minerals a month).

planet_buildings.about: Act 2 planet buildings (Stellaris's). One slot per act2_building_slots_per_pops pops, plus one.

rows.desc: Researchers make research.
Metallurgists make alloys.
Bureaucrats make influence.
Farmers grow food indoors.
Better alloy works.
Entertainers make unity.

ships.about: Act 2 ships (Stellaris's hulls). Power is combat damage per month; hull is how much damage it takes; speed is hyperlane distance per month.

act2_techs.about: Act 2 technologies in Stellaris's tiers (0 = what a civilization knows when it reaches space). A technology needs every one listed in requires; feature: an exotic site whose holder (from Act 1, or in Act 2) may research it. Costs rise with tier and with how strong the effect is.

galaxy_sizes.about: Act 2 galaxy size: star systems per empire (every empire gets one identical spiral arm of this many systems).

rows.name: Tiny
rows.desc: About 9 systems per empire: crowded, borders meet fast.

rows.name: Small
rows.desc: About 12 systems per empire.

rows.name: Medium
rows.desc: About 15 systems per empire: room to grow before borders meet.

rows.name: Large
rows.desc: About 19 systems per empire.

rows.name: Huge
rows.desc: About 24 systems per empire: a long expansion phase.

galaxy_difficulties.about: Act 2 AI difficulty (Stellaris's names). Every AI empire's output is multiplied by ai_mult; aggression scales how readily they declare war.

rows.name: Cadet
rows.desc: AI empires make 35% less and rarely start wars.

rows.name: Ensign
rows.desc: AI empires make 15% less.

rows.name: Captain
rows.desc: AI empires play by the same numbers as you.

rows.name: Commodore
rows.desc: AI empires make 20% more.

rows.name: Admiral
rows.desc: AI empires make 40% more and go to war more readily.

rows.name: Grand Admiral
rows.desc: AI empires make 65% more and are quick to war.

modifiers.about: Every Act 2 bonus: legacy techs, wonders, rare systems, the space race and Act 2 techs. stat is one the game understands (see game_systems).

rows.name: Natural Wonder: Energy
rows.effect_text: +5% Energy while you hold this system

rows.name: Natural Wonder: Minerals
rows.effect_text: +5% Minerals while you hold this system

rows.name: Natural Wonder: Research
rows.effect_text: +5% Research while you hold this system

rows.name: Natural Wonder: Unity
rows.effect_text: +10% Unity while you hold this system

rows.name: Natural Wonder: Plenty
rows.effect_text: +5% Food while you hold this system

rows.name: Regenerative Hull Tissue
rows.effect_text: Ships mend 40 hull a month, even in battle

rows.name: Volatile Mote Storm
rows.effect_text: +10% Ship Damage while you hold it

aliens.about: Stellaris's own empires in Act 2: read from the player's prescripted empires (not human, not machine). aggression is how readily the AI goes to war.

rows.desc: Every non-human, non-machine prescripted empire in the player's Stellaris can appear.

asset_refs.about: Every picture, font and sound the game uses, and where it comes from in the player's own installs. Civ VI icons (ICON_*) and leader pictures are looked up by name and need no row here.

game_systems.about: What comes from each game and how it is read.

rows.what: Civilizations, leaders, colours, city names, techs and their prerequisites, wonders, natural wonders, terrain, text
Tech, wonder, building, project, natural wonder, terrain, leader and civilization icons
Text, sprites, planet classes, portraits, prescripted alien empires, music
